optimize_reason: Highest-priority configuration test: the benchmark net-margin annual change, but peer-ranked inside broad sectors while the platform neutralizes risk at the finer subindustry level. Separating the cross-sectional benchmark (sector) from the risk neutralization (subindustry) preserves the persistent industry-level profitability cycle in the signal instead of differencing it away, while still stripping subindustry risk. Economics: firms whose net margin improves year over year relative to their whole sector are being repriced, because sell-side margin upgrades are incorporated only gradually.

Cash-margin trend ranked against the entire market (widest possible cross-section) with subindustry risk neutralization. Operating cash flow over revenue is the least manipulable profitability measure here; benchmarking it market-wide maximizes cross-sectional dispersion and keeps the durable cash-generation cycle in the signal.

Replace the pro-cyclical revenue denominator with the slow balance-sheet asset base, and use EBIT which strips financing structure and tax regime (critical for cross-region comparability across US GAAP, IFRS and J-GAAP). Revenue in the denominator self-damps genuine profitability improvement: it flattens the signal in expansions and inflates it in contractions. Economics: improving operating return on assets signals real competitive gain that the market prices only gradually.

DuPont confirmation gate: return on assets decomposes into net margin times asset turnover. Only when pricing power AND asset efficiency improve together is the change a genuine operating inflection; a single-leg improvement is usually revenue-recognition timing, inventory capitalisation or a one-off item that reverses next quarter. The product is a confirmation gate, not an average: false positives are pushed toward zero and true positives toward one, sharpening the head of the distribution. The two legs are deliberately low-correlation, unlike net margin versus cash margin which are near-duplicates of the same latent factor.
